title: The Spy Case That Convicted the Wrong Man

scenes.speaker: Maya
scenes.text: He was convicted as a spy. He was innocent.

scenes.speaker: Alex
scenes.text: Meet Alfred Dreyfus, a Jewish officer in the French army. In eighteen-ninety-four, he was wrongly convicted of treason and sent to prison.

scenes.speaker: Maya
scenes.text: The case involved secret evidence, forged documents, and anti-Jewish prejudice. His family and supporters kept challenging it. Later evidence pointed to a different officer.

scenes.speaker: Alex
scenes.text: But correcting the case took years. Dreyfus was finally cleared in nineteen-oh-six. This wasn’t just an argument in a newspaper. A real person lost years of freedom.

scenes.speaker: Maya
scenes.text: The lesson is not that every accusation is false. It’s that someone’s Jewish identity is not proof that they’re disloyal. You still need reliable evidence.
scenes.on_screen: IDENTITY IS NEVER PROOF OF DISLOYALTY

scenes.speaker: Alex
scenes.text: If a case depends on prejudice instead of facts, looking confident doesn’t fix it. Neither does a crowd.

scenes.speaker: Maya
scenes.text: A label is not evidence. Ask what actually happened.
scenes.source: Beyond the Myth · Facts, not scapegoats
